pain_points.description: The task asks for 'merge_to_base if pass, delete_unconditionally if fail'. AUTHORING.md shows no conditional/branching step execution — no `if:`, `when:`, or `on_success:` is documented anywhere. The `check` step's `on_fail:` only supports cancel | continue | retry_loop:<id>. I could not author two cleanup steps where exactly one runs based on `state.tests_pass`. Had to collapse to a single `merge_to_base` cleanup gated by `on_fail: cancel`, which means on failure the worktree is left behind (no `delete_unconditionally` ever runs). The guide should either show a conditional pattern or state explicitly that branching cleanup isn't a v1 concept.

The `until:` value in the example is `state.tests_pass` (bare attribute access), while the `check` example uses `state.tests_pass == True`. Both presumably work, but it's unclear whether `until:` accepts a truthy expression or only an explicit boolean comparison. I went with `== True` for parity with the check example, but a one-line note on what `until:` accepts (any Python expression over `state`?) would remove the doubt.

Inside a loop body, the run-tests step writes `tests_pass`, but it's never spelled out whether that field is re-readable on the *next* iteration's `until:` check (i.e., does loop-body state persist across iterations within the same loop?). The example implies yes, but the §4 state model doesn't discuss loop-iteration semantics at all. I assumed persist-across-iterations because otherwise the loop pattern couldn't work.

The worktree.create example uses `base: $inputs.base_branch` but inputs schema for `base_branch` isn't shown — fine for an example, but a new author has to guess that the input name is free-choice and `base:` accepts any $-substituted string. A one-liner clarifying that would help.

The loop's `run-tests` example uses `command: pytest -x` with no `runtime:`, while §7 step 1 uses `runtime: python` with `script:`. Difference between `command:` (shell) and `script:` (+ runtime) is inferable but never explicitly stated. A sentence on 'command vs script' in §2 would help.

implement.j2 requires `task` (string). I passed `task: "$inputs.feature_description"`. AUTHORING.md §4 says $-substitution happens inside any YAML scalar string including `template_vars:` values, so this should work — but it's not 100% clear whether a bare `$inputs.X` as the *entire* value gets substituted as a string or as the typed input. Since feature_description is already a string this is moot here, but a clarifying example with bare `$inputs.X` (not interpolated into a longer string) would remove ambiguity.

self_assessment: I believe the workflow loads cleanly: it satisfies every load-time rule the guide documents (type: loop is present, writes_files+worktree ancestor satisfied, contract field names match writes, no state_schema declaration, valid worktree actions/policies, valid check on_fail value). The one design compromise is that I could not express the 'delete worktree on fail' branch because the guide shows no conditional execution mechanism; I gated with on_fail: cancel and left a comment explaining the trade-off.
